facts.text: On this date in 1519, Magellan's fleet left Spain to circumnavigate the globe. Only one of his five ships returned — and Magellan himself never made it.
On this date in 1973, Billie Jean King beat Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes. Riggs had boasted no woman could beat him; 90 million people watched him lose.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangladesh than outside it — over half of humanity fits within that single boundary.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding about 20% of the world's fresh surface water within its borders.
The entire population of Australia could fit inside the city limits of Tokyo, with room to spare — Tokyo's metro area holds more people than all of Australia.
On this date in 1873, the New York Stock Exchange closed for 10 days after Jay Cooke & Co. collapsed — the first time the exchange ever shut down due to a financial panic.
On this date in 2008, the SEC temporarily banned short-selling on 799 financial stocks, one of the most sweeping market interventions in Wall Street history.
The Dutch East India Company, often cited as the world's first publicly traded company, was at its peak worth roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars — more than Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia combined.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway owns enough of Coca-Cola that its annual dividend alone — around $776 million — exceeds what Buffett originally paid for the entire stake.

The S&P 500 has historically risen in the month of October so often after a bad September that traders call the turnaround the 'October Effect' — though statistically, October is actually one of the more volatile months, not a reliable rebound.

On this date in 1519, Magellan's fleet left Spain to circumnavigate the Earth. His ships carried no way to measure longitude accurately — they navigated by stars, gut instinct, and survived mostly by luck.
Today in 1854, the Battle of Alma proved that cholera killed more soldiers than combat did. Germ theory didn't yet exist; armies thought bad air was the culprit.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days. The organ doing most of your digestion is, in a meaningful sense, younger than your phone's last software update.
Light leaving the Sun takes eight minutes to reach Earth, but spent roughly 100,000 years fighting its way from the Sun's core to its surface before that sprint even began.
On this day in 1519, Magellan's fleet left Spain to circumnavigate the globe. He never made it back — but his slave, Enrique of Malacca, likely completed the full circle first.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching began at Oxford around 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1973, Billie Jean King defeated Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes. Riggs had beaten the world's top female player months earlier — King practiced by playing men.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is roughly 2,500 years older than she is.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone. You could send a document before you could make a call.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 'The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows,' 2012. Now it feels like it always existed.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or perhaps never had. Untranslatable in one word to English, it carries grief, longing, and belonging simultaneously.

On this day in 1519, Magellan's fleet departed Sanlúcar de Barrameda. The Portuguese verb 'magellanizar' briefly existed, meaning to circumnavigate — a verb built from a man before he'd done the thing.
Petrichor (n.): the smell of rain on dry earth. Coined in 1964 by Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and Richard Thomas, from Greek 'petra' (stone) and 'ichor,' the fluid in the veins of gods.
On this day in 1187, Saladin began the siege of Jerusalem. Arabic preserves the moment: 'fatah' means both conquest and opening — the same word for breaking a city and parting a door.

On this date in 2017, China's central bank declared ICOs illegal, triggering a 40% Bitcoin price drop within days — and yet every project banned that week was outperformed by BTC itself within 18 months.
On this date in 2021, El Salvador's Bitcoin Law survived its first Constitutional Chamber challenge, cementing the first sovereign legal-tender experiment in crypto history.

Ethereum's EIP-1559, deployed in August 2021, has since burned over 4 million ETH permanently — turning a pure inflationary asset into one with a mechanically deflationary supply pressure during high-demand periods.
Satoshi's original Bitcoin whitepaper never uses the word 'blockchain' — the term is a folk contraction of 'chain of blocks' that emerged organically from the developer community after 2010.

The largest single Bitcoin transaction by value was 500,000 BTC moved in November 2011 for a fee of 0.01 BTC — a transfer that would be uneconomical to replicate today purely due to fee market evolution.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need' — the transformer paper. Every major language model today descends from that single architecture.
Today in 2022, DeepMind's AlphaFold database hit 200 million predicted protein structures, covering nearly every known organism — a task structural biology estimated would take centuries by hand.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100 GPUs running for ~90 days. The electricity alone cost an estimated $63 million at US commercial rates.

The first neural network to beat humans at Go, AlphaGo, did so in 2016 using a technique — Monte Carlo tree search guided by learned value functions — that its creators initially considered unpromising.
Modern frontier LLMs can pass the US bar exam in the 90th percentile yet fail trivially rephrased versions of grade-school math problems — a gap that has no clean explanation.
